steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Media representation is how media products portray people, groups, places, events, and ideas — representations are always constructed, never a simple reflection of reality. | Key Fact: Selection and omission: media producers choose what to include and exclude, which shapes how the subject is represented. What is left out is as important as what is included. | Key Fact: Stereotypes are simplified, widely recognised representations of groups — e.g. the 'dumb blonde', the 'action hero', the 'grumpy old man'. They reduce complex identities to a few traits. | Key Fact: Dominant representations are the most common and widely accepted portrayals in society. Alternative representations challenge or subvert these norms.
